chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the woman prays five (times), fasts a month, obeys her husband, and recognizes the right of Ali (peace be upon him), let her enter from whichever door of Paradise she wishes.

key_terms.خَمْساً: Five (referring to the five daily prayers)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a woman to enter Paradise through any door she chooses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the integration of ritual devotion, marital harmony, and specifically the recognition of Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) authority (Haqq) as a decisive factor for female believers' entry into Paradise. In Shia scholarship, the inclusion of 'knowing the right of Ali' underscores the theological principle that correct belief in the Imams is inseparable from righteous action, granting the believer the honor of choosing their own entrance to Paradise. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the interconnection of faith (Iman), worship (Ibadah), and leadership (Imamah).

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the woman Prays five (Prayers a day), and Fasts a month, and obeys her husband, and recognises the right of Ali<sup>asws</sup>, so let her enter from whichever door of the Paradise she so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a woman performs Salat (prayer) five times a day, fasts a month, obeys her husband and recognizes the right of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, she then can enter paradise from whichever door of the garden (paradise) she wants.’”
